why: PV2A (statement-hash scheme 2, holon.ir): F39's rule that every later catalog bump adds catalog_rederivation lines of the same kind assumed that a holon-ir/0.3 statement hash covers rule_catalog_version. From the hash-scheme migration on (python -m holon.statement_diff migrate-hash --milestone M3 --apply, one hash_migration line per law of M2 and M3), every law is under scheme 2, whose hash drops rule_catalog_version: a later bump moves no statement hash, so it adds no catalog_rederivation line (recatalog skips a scheme-2 law and check_entry rejects such a line), and the migration's own registry changes are tied to its hash_migration lines. The catalog lines committed for F30-F39 stay and are still checked under scheme 1 (holon.rules.compute(hash_scheme=1)). No assertion of the file changes: on a migrated scratch tree its tests pass (locally with the committed binding_change proofs' kernel re-runs skipped, F38's mode; TestGate3RunsTheLifecycle needs the pinned checker's GENV, so CI's tests-m3-catalog decides it), and only the module docstring's F39 paragraph gains this rule.

Correction to the F39 line above (PV2A, at the go-ahead): the migration covers M3 only, laws/M3 and laws/M3/derivation (python -m holon.statement_diff migrate-hash --milestone M3 --apply moves only the milestone it names). M2 keeps hash scheme 1: it never bumps its catalog, and spec/M3/lib/lean_promoted.json names its statement hashes. So that line's 'one hash_migration line per law of M2 and M3' reads 'one per law of M3', and its 'every law is under scheme 2' reads 'every M3 law'. Its rule (a bump of scheme-2 laws adds no catalog_rederivation line) and everything else stand.

PV2A (statement-hash scheme 2): holon.statement_diff.append stamps every line it appends with "id" = line_id(line), the sha256 of its canonical JSON, after the check; catalog_rederivation_entries, which this test calls to rebuild the lines, emits none, exactly as it emits no "accepted" record. I86's 136 catalog_rederivation lines (holon-rules/1.6 -> 1.11) are the first catalog lines appended since PV2A, so on I86's landing (#86, CI tests-m3-catalog) all 136 compared unequal on the id alone. The test now masks "id" as it masks "accepted" and checks it apart: a committed line that carries an id must carry its own content's (SD.line_id). Every other comparison (law, hashes, catalogs, reason, the acceptance record regenerated on this tree) is unchanged; F39 has no key, so no fingerprint moves (I67's key: 'F39, no key's test').
